title: China’s homegrown DUV chip tool now has a name: Shanghai Aishengna
excerpt: The state-owned company at the centre of China’s newest chipmaking push finally has a name. Reuters reported on Tuesday that Shanghai Aishengna Electronic Technology Group, a little-known state-owned group, is leading the effort to mass-produce domestically developed immersion deep-ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines, according to a person familiar with the matter who declined to be identified […]
content_html:
The state-owned company at the centre of China’s newest chipmaking push finally has a name. Reuters reported on Tuesday that Shanghai Aishengna Electronic Technology Group, a little-known state-owned group, is leading the effort to mass-produce domestically developed immersion deep-ultraviolet (DUV) lithography machines, according to a person familiar with the matter who declined to be identified because of the sensitivity of the subject.

The company is said to have built its programme by absorbing teams from several of China’s top lithography startups.

The Information first reported on Monday that an unidentified state-backed Shanghai firm had begun manufacturing the machines, and the news alone was enough to send ASML shares down more than 8% at one point on Monday.

Reuters is the first to attach a name to the company, which matters because immersion DUV is a corner of the market ASML has dominated for years, and because Beijing’s push to build it at home is a direct response to the export controls that have kept the Dutch firm’s best tools out of China.

Aishengna itself is obscure, and Reuters’s description of it hoovering up staff from established ventures fits a familiar pattern in China’s chip drive, where the state stitches scattered efforts into a single national champion.

Earlier coverage of China’s DUV progress had pointed to a different Shanghai firm, Yuliangsheng, whose scanner SMIC was said to be testing last year, and which may be one of the teams now folded into the effort.

It helps to be clear about what the machine does. Deep-ultraviolet lithography is the tool that prints circuit patterns onto silicon, and the immersion variant slips a thin layer of water between the lens and the wafer so it can etch finer features.

It sits a generation behind extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, the far more advanced technology that ASML alone produces and that China has been blocked from buying. DUV cannot match EUV on the most cutting-edge chips, but paired with a technique called multi-patterning it can still reach fairly advanced nodes, which is how SMIC has been able to turn out 7nm processors without any EUV at all. Multi-patterning is slower, costlier, and tends to lower yields, so it is a workaround rather than a substitute.

The caveats are heavy, and Reuters’s source stressed them. Aishengna’s machine is expected to need further testing and remains far from matching ASML’s competing models, so it poses no immediate commercial threat to a company that still supplies most of the world’s advanced lithography.

This is a source-based account rather than an official one, and none of the companies involved have confirmed it on the record.

What a homegrown line would buy China, if it works, is insurance. Domestic DUV would give the country’s chipmakers an alternative source of equipment should Western governments tighten the rules further, whether by restricting exports outright or by cutting off the servicing that keeps existing foreign machines running.

The Information, citing two people, said the first units are due to be delivered this year to leading Chinese manufacturers including SMIC, Hua Hong Semiconductor, and the memory-chip maker ChangXin Memory Technologies.

China’s drive toward domestic silicon has already reshaped how it designs AI chips, and lithography is the harder, more strategic frontier.

For Beijing the symbolism is considerable, since semiconductor self-sufficiency is one of Xi Jinping’s highest priorities and lithography has been the most stubborn gap in the country’s supply chain.

ASML, whose stock has since steadied, did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and neither did SMIC, Hua Hong, or CXMT.

content_html_zh:
这家处于中国最新芯片制造发展中心的国有公司终于有了名字。 路透社周二报道称，据一位因此事敏感性而拒绝透露姓名的知情人士透露，上海艾圣纳电子科技集团是一家鲜为人知的国有企业，正在牵头大规模生产国产开发的浸没式深紫外（DUV）光刻机。

据称，该公司是通过吸收中国几家顶级光刻初创公司的团队来制定其计划的。

《The Information》周一首次报道称，一家身份不明的、由政府支持的上海公司已开始生产这些机器，仅这一消息就足以导致 ASML 股价周一一度下跌超过 8%。

路透社是第一个给该公司命名的公司，这很重要，因为浸入式 DUV 是 ASML 多年来主导的市场一角，而且北京推动在国内生产该公司是对出口管制的直接反应，出口管制使这家荷兰公司最好的工具无法进入中国。

艾胜纳本身并不为人所知，路透社对它从老牌企业吸纳员工的描述符合中国芯片驱动领域的常见模式，即国家将分散的努力整合到一个国家冠军企业中。

早些时候对中国 DUV 进展的报道指出了另一家上海公司 Yuliangsheng，据说该公司的扫描仪中芯国际去年正在进行测试，该公司可能是现在参与这项工作的团队之一。

这有助于清楚机器的用途。 深紫外光刻是将电路图案印刷到硅上的工具，浸入式光刻在透镜和晶圆之间涂上一层薄薄的水，这样就可以蚀刻出更精细的特征。

它比极紫外 (EUV) 光刻技术落后一代，这是 ASML 独自生产的先进技术，但中国已被禁止购买。 在最尖端的芯片上，DUV 无法与 EUV 相媲美，但与多重图案化技术配合使用，它仍然可以达到相当先进的节点，这就是中芯国际能够在完全不使用 EUV 的情况下生产 7 纳米处理器的原因。 多重图案化速度较慢，成本较高，而且产量往往较低，因此它是一种解决方法，而不是替代品。

这些警告很严重，路透社的消息人士也强调了这一点。 艾圣纳的机器预计需要进一步测试，并且距离与 ASML 的竞争型号相距甚远，因此它不会对仍然供应全球大部分先进光刻机的公司构成直接的商业威胁。

这是一个基于消息来源的账户，而不是官方账户，并且没有一家相关公司在记录中证实这一点。

如果可行的话，本土生产线将为中国带来的就是保险。 如果西方政府进一步收紧规则，无论是通过彻底限制出口还是通过切断维持现有外国机器运行的服务，国内 DUV 将为该国的芯片制造商提供替代的设备来源。

《The Information》援引两名知情人士的话称，首批设备将于今年交付给中芯国际、华虹半导体和存储芯片制造商长鑫存储科技等中国领先制造商。

中国对国产芯片的推动已经重塑了其人工智能芯片的设计方式，而光刻技术是更难、更具战略意义的前沿领域。

对于北京来说，这一象征意义重大，因为半导体自给自足是习近平的最高优先事项之一，而光刻机一直是该国供应链中最顽固的缺口。

ASML 的股价此后趋于稳定，但没有立即回应置评请求，中芯国际、华虹或长鑫存储也没有立即回应置评请求。
